concepts.name: Real Number System
concepts.description: The real number system consists of rational and irrational numbers. It provides a complete framework for representing quantities on the number line.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify numbers as rational or irrational and identify them as members of the real number system.

concepts.name: Properties of Real Numbers
concepts.description: Real numbers obey fundamental arithmetic properties such as closure, commutativity, associativity and distributivity, which simplify mathematical operations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply the basic properties of real numbers to simplify numerical expressions.

concepts.name: Prime Factorization
concepts.description: Every composite number can be expressed uniquely as a product of prime numbers, apart from the order of the factors.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the prime factorization of any composite number.

concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
concepts.description: The theorem guarantees the uniqueness of the prime factorization of every integer greater than one. It forms the basis for many number theory applications.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic in mathematical problems.

concepts.name: Applications of Prime Factorization
concepts.description: Prime factorization is used to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF), Least Common Multiple (LCM), and to solve divisibility-related problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the HCF and LCM of two or more numbers using prime factorization.

concepts.name: Irrational Numbers
concepts.description: Irrational numbers cannot be expressed as the ratio of two integers and have non-terminating, non-repeating decimal expansions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish irrational numbers from rational numbers based on their decimal representation.

concepts.name: Decimal Expansion of Real Numbers
concepts.description: The decimal expansion of a rational number either terminates or repeats, whereas that of an irrational number is non-terminating and non-repeating.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the nature of a real number from its decimal expansion.

concepts.name: Relationship Between Rational and Irrational Numbers
concepts.description: Operations involving rational and irrational numbers produce different types of results depending on the operation and operands.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to predict and justify whether the result of operations involving rational and irrational numbers is rational or irrational.

concepts.name: Key Ideas of Real Numbers
concepts.description: The chapter consolidates concepts including the real number system, unique prime factorization, and properties of irrational numbers.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to summarize the major concepts of the chapter and connect them to problem-solving situations.
